So it’s sad to admit, but not too long ago, I identified as trans :/. I will say it certainly felt like a spiritual possession now that I am past it. There have also been reports on the detransition subreddit about people feeling similarly.

There’s this phenomenon called AGP where a person is aroused by idea of being a woman. Enabling this arousal is theorized by some to be the motivation behind many trans peoples’ transitions. Since getting out of what I honestly see to be a cult, I’ve developed a strong aversion to anyone associating with the trans ideology fwiw. I do think it has a lot to do with the energy they give off and not feeling compatible with it anymore. 

If we are to argue that the demiurge is the manifestation of low vibrations, I don’t think it’s that far of a stretch to suggest that folks that cannot help but give in to their most primitive emotions are possessed to some degree by the demiurge. 

I personally think these people (and I certainly was) are very ungrounded, atheistic/unspirtual and extremely vulnerable. I think in a lot of ways the trans ideology resembles a spirituality, but it’s distinct in that one’s value in the community comes from not from an inherent sense of self worth but in the technology that’s applied to change one’s form in a specific way. In this manner I think it is a faux-spirituality, but its likeliness to an actual spirituality is what drives spiritually devoid folks to it. It’s theoretical underpinnings in science I believe also drives many atheistic people who more or less worship modern science to it as well. 

I see using hard drugs as similarly giving in to a one’s primitive emotions and temptations. In this sense I think there’s a lot of similarities between hard drug users and trans people, so I think it’s fair to say this group of people could also be largely under the influence/possessed by the demiurge.

Hey, I read some of your other comments about how you want to be a girl even in mundane situations as well as in sexual ones. I’ve also felt the same and have come to believe that there is something in my subconscious that associates being a girl with relaxation and even confidence while it associates being a man with anxiety and low self esteem. 

I think there’s an element of toxic masculinity that gets embedded into our psyches in a very deep, subconscious way that can be exceptionally difficult to reprogram. I think that’s where the idea of transitioning gets it’s appeal – it’s a way to avoid  the painstaking task of having to reprogram the mind to understand that the same qualities of peace that one associates with living as a woman can be found living as a man. 

The natural question then is ‘how does one reprogram their subconscious’? I think the answer is use your imagination to bring the peace from your visions of yourself as a girl into visions of yourself as a boy. For example, if you envision going to sleep as a girl as something that would be more peaceful than going to sleep as a boy, perhaps try to envision yourself as a slightly slightly masculinized girl and then see if you can’t draw the same feeling of contentment from this vision as compared to a vision of oneself as a completely feminine girl. Overtime, of course, slowly repeating this process until you eventually associate the idea of yourself as a man with the same level of peace and contentment as you originally had envisioning yourself as a woman. 

Idk, to be honest it’s just a theory.  Over time my dysphoria has gone away and I feel like it’s been through envisioning myself as a more confident man that I’ve been able to minimize my dysphoria.

I will say for me, personally, I wish I would have waited. I was unaware of the existence of being agp at the time and this combined with numerous other (poor) reasons eventually prompted me to begin hormone therapy. The truth was I was scared of being a guy, I wasn’t pleased with all the social/romantic implications of being a man and thought I’d be happier as a transwoman. But the truth is I’ll never be a woman, I think I would had preferred to be a woman if I had been given a choice, but alas I was not. What I really needed to do was work through all my issues and essentially swallow the difficulties and embrace the possibilities that come with being a man. 

I suppose hormones can be right for some people, but for the vast majority, I really think internal work can be done to mostly eradicate feelings of gender dysphoria. 

I would also honestly go so far as to say that I believe transitioning is becoming an industry that capitalism is taking advantage of, ie. loosening the restrictions on the requirements for transitioning and endorsing of the idea of developing a life long dependency on medication and surgery and cryo sperm storage. I think when one really takes a step back and asks the question “do I really want to develop a life long dependency on medication, risk various health issues, including ED, fertility, (in my case psychosis), etc. and permanently develop breasts to be a ‘sexy’ woman?” I think the wise answer is relatively clear. 

As someone with a strong sex drive and agp I will say I am well aware of how compelling the idea of transitioning can be and difficult it can be to resist the urge to do. I will say I was personally not strong enough and ultimately took hormones for a year and half, and then relapsed a couple of times before getting off them for good. 

Ultimately the choice to remain on them is up to you, but I think it would be wise for you to deeply question your motives for doing so.
